elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: Inserted § 5.4: "IBM, as the Customer under this Agreement, may terminate this Agreement for convenience upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to MSL". IBM is the Customer/buyer party per the preamble, so the Agreement-level convenience right is granted in operative language (the disjunctive "or an Order Form" is not required).

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: "upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to MSL" — exactly 30 days, written, and no additional conditions or consents attached.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: "MSL shall refund to IBM, on a pro rata basis, any fees prepaid by IBM for the period after the effective date of termination" — the refund is expressly pro rata (not merely post-termination-period), runs from Vendor to Customer, and is triggered by the convenience termination.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: Already met in the base text: the three-year term continues "unless terminated as provided in Section 5.0," and § 5.1 permits termination "by either Party for cause" only. The six-month (Base) / twelve-month (SOW) notices operate against automatic renewal and are natural-term non-renewal assessed under RENEWAL, not a mid-term Vendor convenience right; the ancillary confidentiality-exchange notice right terminates only that separate agreement.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: The inserted right runs on thirty (30) days' notice, which is shorter than (and more favourable than) the 60–90 day fallback window; the fallback wording is therefore not the drafted position.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: No cap is added, and the retained Section 5 charge mechanic ("The price for Parts, whether in inventory or on order to meet IBM's forecasted requirements, shall be an amount equal to MSL's cost") plus § 6.1's preserved "cost reimbursements under the Price section" remain uncapped.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Nothing ties any MSL termination effective date to the end of the then-current term; the auto-renewal clause simply lets "either Party" give notice of intent to terminate, which under the stated boundary does not itself make Vendor termination term-end-only.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: The only MSL notice mechanic is the six (6) months' written notice against renewal in the term clause (twelve (12) months under the SOW Attachment), both of which exceed 90 days.

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: the single inserted § 5.4 supplies the Customer convenience right, the 30-day written notice, and the pro-rata prepaid-fee refund, and the Vendor-side element is already satisfied because Section 5.0 gives MSL only for-cause termination during the committed three-year term.

The deterministic check "Customer convenience termination present: false" is a false negative on literal string matching: the clause names the terminating party as "IBM, as the Customer under this Agreement," rather than the token "Customer," and IBM is the buyer party in the preamble. Substantively the right is present and operative.

Minimality holds: one concise insertion, no deletions, no survival tail, no at-own-expense or damages add-ons, and correctly no "in whole or in part" language (no Order Form/partial-termination structure in the selected checklist). The clarifying phrase "as the Customer under this Agreement" is justified because "Customer" is not a defined term here (the Agreement uses "Customer Orders" for IBM's own customers), so it prevents ambiguity rather than adding a requirement.

Intent preserved: the new subsection sits inside Section 5, so the term clause's "unless terminated as provided in Section 5.0" cross-reference and the SOW Attachment's reference to "Section 5.0 of the Base Agreement" remain intact; the for-cause regime, the renewal-notice mechanic, and § 6.1's purchase-order cancellation and cost-reimbursement allocation all survive without contradiction.

Residual point for the drafter (not a completeness defect against this checklist): the retained Section 5 parts/inventory cost-reimbursement mechanic can operate as a de facto exit charge on a convenience termination. The preferred elements do not require a fee cap, so removing or capping it would exceed the checklist; if negotiation counsel wants certainty, raise it as a separate comment rather than an edit here.
Finding status "deviation" is correct: before the edit there was no Customer convenience exit in a three-year term, which the rule treats as a deviation (missing behaviour).
